name: Calculator
description: An expression calculator with a running history, plus Base64 / URL encoding and MD5
author: Lattice

config.label: Keep a history
config.help: Off hides the list and stops writing it. Nothing already saved is deleted.

sections.title: Typing a sum
items: Type the whole expression, not one key at a time: 12*(3+4)-5. The answer updates as you type.
Enter commits it: the answer moves into the box so you can keep going, and the sum goes into the history.
Esc clears the box. Backspace does what you expect — this is a text field, not a keypad.

sections.title: What the operators do
items: % is modulo, not percent: 17%5 is 2. A percentage is just /100 written out.
Parentheses work as usual; a leading minus is allowed, and -3^2 is -(3^2).

sections.title: The history
items: Click a row to put that answer back in the box — the sum stays visible next to it.
History entries is how many rows fit; Keep a history off hides the list without deleting it.
It is stored per widget, so two calculators on one desktop share one history.

sections.title: Encode and Hash
items: Encode turns text into Base64 or a percent-encoded URL, and back. Base64 is UTF-8 safe, so Chinese survives the round trip.
Hash gives you MD5 of the text — lowercase hex. WebCrypto has no MD5, so this one is computed in the widget.
Copy puts the result on the clipboard. The clipboard permission is separate: without it the text is selected instead.

sections.title: When it says error
items: Cannot divide by zero and Unbalanced parentheses are the two the parser will tell you about by name.
Anything else shows Unexpected character with the character in question.

changes: First release: expression calculator with live results and a clickable history.
Base64 and URL encoding, both directions, UTF-8 safe.
MD5 of the typed text, computed in the widget.
